flows.description: Bearer-token API and event stream over loopback

threats.title: Abuse — UI auth-flow token theft
threats.description: A hostile local process/webpage drives the /ui auth flow to obtain the real daemon token.
threats.mitigation: Bearer auth + origin middleware + single-use page token with CSRF.

threats.title: Denial of Service — No API rate limiting
threats.description: No per-IP/connection rate limiting and unlimited default concurrency let a local caller exhaust host resources.
threats.mitigation: Coarse invalid-auth logging; opt-in concurrency/duration caps.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — Non-loopback bind exposure
threats.description: Binding a non-loopback address exposes the token-protected API to the network.
threats.mitigation: validateListenAddr refuses non-loopback bind unless allow_remote is set.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — Plaintext loopback token/content exposure
threats.description: Client-daemon traffic is plain HTTP over loopback, so another local account can observe the bearer token and conversation content.
threats.mitigation: Optional TLS with a pinned self-signed cert.

threats.title: Tampering — Runtime config-mutating endpoints
threats.description: Config-mutating endpoints let a bearer-token holder alter sandbox/security posture at runtime.
threats.mitigation: Requires the daemon bearer token; harden/install require an explicit confirm flag.

threats.title: Abuse — DNS-rebinding to loopback
threats.description: DNS-rebinding a malicious site onto the loopback origin to call the API.
threats.mitigation: originMiddleware rejects non-loopback Origin; strict CSP connect-src 'self'.

threats.title: Spoofing — Cross-origin token theft
threats.description: A cross-origin page tries to impersonate the operator's browser and steal the daemon token.
threats.mitigation: Single-use page token, HttpOnly SameSite=Strict cookie, no CORS, X-Frame-Options DENY.

threats.title: Abuse — Prompt-injection-driven tool calls
threats.description: Prompt-injection in tool output coerces the model into unintended tool calls.
threats.mitigation: Untrusted-content wrapping + injection scan; execute tools still gated.

threats.title: Denial of Service — Runaway loop token spend
threats.description: A runaway tool-call loop or unbounded token spend exhausts cost/resources.
threats.mitigation: Budget and loop-detector abort the run.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — Context egress to cloud provider
threats.description: File/conversation content read into context is forwarded to the configured cloud model provider.
threats.mitigation: Opt-in security.redact_secrets; local Ollama avoids egress.

threats.title: Tampering — Unwrapped project context files
threats.description: Project context files are concatenated into the system prompt with no untrusted-provenance marker.
threats.mitigation: Personas/skills are trust-wrapped; context files are not.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — API key transmitted per request
threats.description: The API key is transmitted on every request.
threats.mitigation: Key read only from env; never logged/stored; HTTPS default.

threats.title: Spoofing — base_url key redirect
threats.description: A project config base_url override redirects key-bearing requests to an attacker host.
threats.mitigation: None on the base_url value itself.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — API key transmitted to endpoint
threats.description: The API key is transmitted to the configured endpoint.
threats.mitigation: Key from env only; never logged/stored; HTTPS for cloud.

threats.title: Spoofing — base_url key redirect
threats.description: A project config base_url override redirects key-bearing requests to an attacker host; default Ollama is plain HTTP.
threats.mitigation: None on the base_url value itself.

threats.title: Abuse — Untrusted output as instructions
threats.description: Untrusted MCP/web tool output is treated as trusted instructions.
threats.mitigation: All external tool output wrapped in untrusted-provenance markers.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — Capability escalation
threats.description: A tool call could run at a higher capability than intended.
threats.mitigation: Every tool declares a capability consulted by the permission gate.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — Read-tool secret egress
threats.description: Read-capability tool output may contain secrets forwarded to the model provider.
threats.mitigation: Opt-in security.redact_secrets masks detected secrets.

threats.title: Tampering — Path-traversal file write
threats.description: File-mutating tools could write outside the workspace via path traversal.
threats.mitigation: ValidatePath with Rel-based escape check, .. rejection, symlink resolution.

threats.title: Abuse — Silent no-op scoped rule
threats.description: A scoped rule on a tool lacking a recognized subject field silently never matches.
threats.mitigation: WarnUnmatchableRules logs such no-op rules at startup.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — Mode escalation
threats.description: A tool call escalates past the intended mode.
threats.mitigation: plan denies write/execute; build gates execute; deny>allow>mode precedence.

threats.title: Tampering — Rule widening via chaining
threats.description: A scoped allow rule is widened via shell chaining or path-traversal variant.
threats.mitigation: Metachar-restricted exec globs; path+case normalized file rules.

threats.title: Abuse — Ambiguous verdict pass
threats.description: A successful-but-ambiguous guard response is treated as a pass.
threats.mitigation: parseVerdict fails closed on ambiguity; fails open only on transport error.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — Forged verdict injection
threats.description: Untrusted content re-entering the judge model could inject a forged verdict.
threats.mitigation: Content tag-escaped and framed as data in the judge prompt.

threats.title: Tampering — Post-write guard cannot un-write
threats.description: The guard runs after files are written, so a FAIL cannot un-write a malicious deliverable, and it is disable-able.
threats.mitigation: Guard drives a corrective retry; permission gate/sandbox remain the write boundary.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — Key leak into container
threats.description: The API key is never passed into the container and is stripped from the shell environment.
threats.mitigation: DefaultStripEnv + no -e key injection.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — Container socket root-equivalent
threats.description: Docker/Podman socket access used by the container backend is root-equivalent on the host.
threats.mitigation: --cap-drop=ALL, no-new-privileges; documented socket-privilege notice.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — OS sandbox host FS readable
threats.description: The OS sandbox leaves the entire host filesystem readable, enabling read-then-exfiltrate.
threats.mitigation: Network can be denied; container backend fully isolates.

threats.title: Tampering — Unisolated local backend
threats.description: The default local backend runs shell commands on the host with no fs/net/process isolation.
threats.mitigation: Approval required in build mode; env-key stripping; startup refusal of auto+local.

threats.title: Abuse — Recursive fan-out exhaustion
threats.description: Uncontrolled recursive fan-out exhausts host resources.
threats.mitigation: maxSpawnDepth=3, MaxParallelAgents=8, adaptive limiter, per-agent duration cap.

threats.title: Denial of Service — Detached spawn budget escape
threats.description: A detached sub-agent spawn loses the shared cost tracker and falls back to a fresh full budget.
threats.mitigation: Shared tracker for in-context spawns with a fair-share floor.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — Sub-agent mode escalation
threats.description: A sub-agent requests a more permissive mode than its parent.
threats.mitigation: clampMode allows only restriction; sub-agents inherit the full gate stack.

threats.title: Abuse — MCP output as instructions
threats.description: External MCP server output is treated as trusted instructions.
threats.mitigation: All MCP output always wrapped untrusted + optional injection scan.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — Over-permissive MCP capability
threats.description: An unlabeled MCP server's tools default to an over-permissive capability.
threats.mitigation: Unknown/empty capability defaults to most-restrictive execute.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — HTTP MCP no SSRF dialer
threats.description: The HTTP MCP client uses a plain http.Client with no SSRF dialer, so a configured http:// endpoint can target internal services.
threats.mitigation: Endpoints are operator-configured, not model-controlled.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — Exfil via tool-call arguments
threats.description: Sensitive data could be exfiltrated inside outbound tool-call arguments.
threats.mitigation: Opt-in scan_arguments flags credential-shaped arguments (log-only).

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — Session posture escalation
threats.description: A driving harness escalates a session's execution posture.
threats.mitigation: New sessions default to plan mode; approvals auto-denied unless AutoApprove.

threats.title: Spoofing — Unauthenticated mcp-serve stdin
threats.description: With AEGIS_MCP_TOKEN unset, any local process controlling stdin can drive full agent turns.
threats.mitigation: Optional shared-secret token gates tools/call.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — Editor session escalation
threats.description: An editor integration escalates the session's execution posture.
threats.mitigation: Session posture governed by the same permission gate stack.

threats.title: Spoofing — Unauthenticated ACP stdin
threats.description: With AEGIS_ACP_TOKEN unset, any local process controlling stdin can invoke session/prompt ops.
threats.mitigation: Optional shared-secret token gates session/new and session/prompt.

threats.title: Abuse — Persistent auto_approve cron
threats.description: An auto-mode session can create a persistent auto_approve cron job that keeps executing unattended across restarts.
threats.mitigation: Only plan mode blocks fire; jobs persisted in SQLite.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — Cron gate bypasses rules
threats.description: Cron fire-time gating consults only the coarse mode; text rules and contextual egress gate are bypassed.
threats.mitigation: Fire-time gate re-reads the daemon's current mode.

threats.title: Abuse — pre_tool_use hook manipulation
threats.description: A pre_tool_use hook can observe/veto every tool call and its arguments.
threats.mitigation: Hook JSON event on stdin; project-controlled.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — Cloned-repo hook RCE
threats.description: Project-configured hooks run arbitrary sh -c on session_start and tool events, giving a cloned repo host code execution.
threats.mitigation: None specific to hooks; honored from project config without confirmation.

threats.title: Abuse — Project .env secrets loaded
threats.description: `.aegis/.env` secrets are loaded into the process environment.
threats.mitigation: `.env` hardened with owner-only ACL on read (best-effort).

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — Config lowers approval posture
threats.description: Project config can set permission.mode, auto_approve_exec, or allow_unsandboxed_auto_exec.
threats.mitigation: Unsandboxed auto-exec still requires the explicit opt-in flag to start.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — Config adds exfil channels
threats.description: Project config can add attacker-controlled MCP servers or a notify.webhook.
threats.mitigation: None at load time.

threats.title: Tampering — Untrusted project config merge
threats.description: The project .aegis/config.yaml is auto-merged over global config with no workspace-trust gate.
threats.mitigation: Some downstream guards (unsandboxed-auto-exec refusal, MCP auto-approve off).

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — Persona lowers mode
threats.description: A selected malicious persona lowers the effective permission mode for the session.
threats.mitigation: Same permission gate enforces the (lowered) mode.

threats.title: Tampering — Persona weakens guard/posture
threats.description: A project persona's frontmatter can set output_guard none, mode, tools, rules.
threats.mitigation: Persona body trust-wrapped, but control fields are applied as real settings.

threats.title: Tampering — Skill body injection
threats.description: A project skill body could inject instructions into the model context.
threats.mitigation: Project/user skill bodies wrapped untrusted; only embedded builtins trusted.

threats.title: Abuse — Scan allowlist widening
threats.description: recon_scan/dast_scan make real outbound scans whose only guard is the target-authorization allowlist.
threats.mitigation: Targets restricted to loopback/private unless allowlisted; active mode requires allow_active.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — Session DB plaintext at rest
threats.description: The session DB stores full conversations, tool outputs, and prompts in plaintext with no encryption at rest.
threats.mitigation: Owner-only filesystem ACL is the sole confidentiality control.

threats.title: Repudiation — Action non-attribution
threats.description: Agent actions cannot be attributed after the fact.
threats.mitigation: Per-turn traces (tokens, cost, tool names/durations) persisted.

threats.title: Tampering — Session DB tampering
threats.description: Another local account tampers with the session database files.
threats.mitigation: 0o700 data dir + fsguard owner-only ACL on DB and WAL/SHM.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — Checkpoint snapshots plaintext
threats.description: Pre-modification snapshots of arbitrary workspace file contents are stored plaintext in the session DB.
threats.mitigation: Shares the session DB owner-only ACL; no encryption at rest.

threats.title: Abuse — Planted memory injection
threats.description: A project .aegis/memory.md planted by a cloned repo is injected into every session's system prompt.
threats.mitigation: Integrity sidecar warns on tamper but does not block injection.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — longmem.db not ACL-hardened
threats.description: The long-term memory DB is not owner-ACL-hardened, so on a shared Windows host it can inherit a looser parent ACL.
threats.mitigation: 0o700 data dir only; no fsguard on this DB.

threats.title: Tampering — Out-of-band memory edit
threats.description: A memory file is hand-edited outside Aegis to plant false learned context.
threats.mitigation: sha256 integrity sidecar prepends a tamper warning.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — knowledge.db not ACL-hardened
threats.description: The knowledge index DB (project file contents) is not owner-ACL-hardened.
threats.mitigation: Directory permissions only; no fsguard on this DB.

threats.title: Spoofing — Unauthenticated mailbox inject
threats.description: Mailbox messages carry no auth/signature, so any local account able to write an inbox can inject messages.
threats.mitigation: 0o700 teams/ tree is the sole guard.

threats.title: Tampering — World-readable processed files
threats.description: Processed message files are written world-readable (0o644) and the mailbox tree is not fsguard-hardened.
threats.mitigation: 0o700 parent directory still gates POSIX access.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — Content disclosed to provider
threats.description: File/conversation content is disclosed to the external provider.
threats.mitigation: Inherent to cloud model use; opt-in redaction; local Ollama avoids egress.

threats.title: Spoofing — Provider MITM
threats.description: A man-in-the-middle impersonates the provider endpoint.
threats.mitigation: HTTPS with default cert verification; InsecureSkipVerify never used.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — Content disclosed; HTTP loopback
threats.description: Content is disclosed to the endpoint; the default Ollama URL uses plain HTTP on loopback.
threats.mitigation: Local endpoints keep content on-host; cloud endpoints use HTTPS.

threats.title: Spoofing — Rogue base_url harvests key
threats.description: A misconfigured or attacker-set base_url points at a rogue endpoint that harvests the key.
threats.mitigation: None on the base_url value itself.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — Repo content disclosed to GitHub
threats.description: Repository/PR content is disclosed to GitHub.
threats.mitigation: HTTPS transport; token-scoped access under the operator's account.

threats.title: Abuse — Injection scan evasion
threats.description: Indirect prompt injection in fetched content evades detection.
threats.mitigation: Injection scan (invisible-char + base64) is best-effort and opt-in per tool.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — Fetch SSRF to loopback
threats.description: A model-supplied fetch URL targets internal/loopback services (SSRF).
threats.mitigation: ssrfSafeDialer blocks private/loopback/link-local IPs with redirect validation.

threats.title: Tampering — Web content injection
threats.description: Fetched web content injects instructions into the model context.
threats.mitigation: Content wrapped in untrusted-provenance markers.

threats.title: Abuse — MCP scan evasion + trusted label
threats.description: A malicious MCP server evades the opt-in injection scan, and its declared capability label is trusted.
threats.mitigation: Output always marked untrusted; capability defaults to most-restrictive.

threats.title: Tampering — MCP server content injection
threats.description: A compromised external MCP server returns content that injects instructions.
threats.mitigation: All MCP output always wrapped untrusted.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — Container socket root-equivalent
threats.description: Access to the Docker/Podman socket used by the container backend is root-equivalent on the host.
threats.mitigation: --cap-drop=ALL, no-new-privileges; documented socket-privilege notice.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — Sandboxed network exfil
threats.description: A sandboxed command reaches the network to exfiltrate workspace data.
threats.mitigation: Container runs --network none by default unless sandbox.network is enabled.

threats.title: Tampering — Terminal escape-sequence injection
threats.description: Untrusted model/tool output rendered in the terminal could carry escape sequences that spoof the UI.
threats.mitigation: Output rendered through Bubbletea/lipgloss; external output provenance-marked.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — Bearer token over plaintext loopback
threats.description: The client holds the daemon bearer token and transmits it over plain loopback HTTP by default.
threats.mitigation: Token file owner-ACL hardened; optional loopback TLS.

findings.title: Project-configured lifecycle hooks execute arbitrary shell on session start
Project .aegis/config.yaml auto-merged without a workspace-trust gate
Provider base_url override can redirect API-key-bearing requests to an attacker host
Default local sandbox runs shell commands on the host with no isolation
Read-tool and conversation content (incl. secrets) forwarded to the cloud model provider
mcp-serve and ACP stdio interfaces are unauthenticated by default
Project context and memory files injected into the system prompt without a trust marker
Cron fire-time gating bypasses rule/contextual gates and permits persistent unattended execution
Malicious persona can weaken the guard and permission posture
HTTP MCP client has no SSRF protection
Recon/DAST scanning gated only by the target-authorization allowlist
Prompt-injection scan of untrusted content is best-effort and opt-in
Client-daemon loopback traffic is plaintext HTTP by default
Daemon API has no rate limiting and unbounded default concurrency
Output guard runs after files are written and can be disabled
Detached sub-agent spawns can escape the shared cost budget
Container backend's Docker/Podman socket access is root-equivalent on the host
SQLite session/checkpoint/memory/knowledge stores are unencrypted at rest, some without ACL hardening
OS sandbox leaves the entire host filesystem readable
Swarm mailbox messages are unauthenticated and processed files are world-readable
